summary: Cleaned up and rewrote the codex extension's usage-service test file (including a 401 no-cache-failure test and a raw-content auth helper), registered the codex extension in gizmo.registry.json, replaced the unresolvable @gizmo/extensions import in the server index with a local mirror interface, ran prettier over codex files (including the .svelte panel via prettier-plugin-svelte), verified pnpm check/format/test pass (14 new tests, 158 total), rebuilt the web bundle, and installed the extension via directory junction + web bundle copy matching Gizmo's linking pattern.
decisions: Added a homeWithRaw helper so the 'not valid JSON' auth test can write a literal non-JSON string instead of going through JSON.stringify via homeWith.
Mirrored GizmoServerExtension as a local interface in extensions/codex/src/server/index.ts because @gizmo/extensions is not resolvable from inside the registry repo, avoiding a TS2307 type error.

Installed the extension by creating a Windows directory junction at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/codex pointing at the registry's extensions/codex and copying codex.web.js to ~/.pi/agent/extension-web/codex.web.js, replicating Gizmo's documented linking behaviour.
Left all changes uncommitted in the gizmo-registry repo so the user can review before committing.
errors: Initial edit on usage-service.test.ts mangled indentation (the it() block lost proper tab nesting), causing a follow-up edit's oldText match to fail.
An attempted registry-catalog edit failed because the oldText didn't match the actual JSON; resolved by re-reading gizmo.registry.json and editing the correct location.

pnpm check reported TS2307 (Cannot find module '@gizmo/extensions') and several TS7006 implicit-any errors in extensions/codex/src/server/index.ts; resolved by replacing the import with a local interface and typing the parameters.
Prettier CLI couldn't infer a parser for CodexPanel.svelte via the codex/** glob; resolved by invoking prettier --plugin prettier-plugin-svelte directly on the .svelte file.
